# ruststream-zeromq

> `ruststream-zeromq` is the ZeroMQ broker crate for RustStream, a Rust framework for services that subscribe to message brokers and publish to them. It joins a service to a ZeroMQ topology over the pure-Rust `zeromq` client on the `tcp://` and `ipc://` transports, with no server in the middle and a documented frame layout, so the peer on the other side does not have to be Rust.

A service picks one of three patterns: `ZmqQueue` (PUSH/PULL, competing consumers), `ZmqFanout` (PUB/SUB, broadcast filtered by name prefix) or `ZmqRpc` (DEALER/ROUTER, request and reply), each on a `ZmqEndpoint` that says whether this process binds or connects. A subscription is a plain name, `#[subscriber("jobs")]`. A routes file imports its pattern's prelude (`ruststream_zeromq::queue::prelude::*` and so on), which offers that pattern's publish policy as `Publish`; a file mounting more than one pattern imports `ruststream_zeromq::prelude::*`.

This site holds the guides, one page per component and the architecture of the crate; the API reference is on docs.rs, and the framework itself is documented on the RustStream site.
